root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Alekhine Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Bd3

overview: After the Caro-Kann Classical exchanges, 5.Bd3 leaves the d4 pawn en prise: Black can take it with ...Qxd4, and White hopes for rapid development with Nf3, Nxf6+ and Qe2 or Bxh7 ideas against the queen and king. Black can also decline with ...Nxe4 or ...e6 and keep a sound Caro-Kann structure. It is a rare sideline and the evidence is thin, so this is read from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bd3, Qe2 and Nf3, castle and attack
Use the open e-file and pressure on h7
Recapture and keep a lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Take the d4 pawn with ...Qxd4 and use the queen carefully
Or trade knights on e4 and play ...Nd7 and ...e6
Use the sound Caro structure to defend

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file with White bishop on d3
Black solid c6/e6 pawns against White centre

character.notes: The gambit invites forcing play with open lines and threats against h7.

gambit.notes: White leaves the d4 pawn for development and attacking chances; Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Black can take material and defend with the sound Caro structure, so the compensation is doubtful.

structure.notes: Pieces fight on open lines after the exchanges on e4.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose this White gambit.

level.notes: Moves are simple to learn, but the gambit is dubious so not a beginner choice.
